title: Scaling joint Kolmogorov-complexity profiles
reason: Scaling complete algorithmic-information profiles asks whether shared information has a universal homogeneous geometry, across arbitrary tuples rather than one example.
formal: For every fixed integer k≥1 and real λ>0, does there exist a constant c>0 such that, for every integer n≥2 and every tuple of binary strings a₁,…,a_k of length at most n, there are finite binary strings b₁,…,b_k satisfying |C(b_S)−λ C(a_S)|≤c log₂ n for every nonempty S⊆{1,…,k}? The same tuple b must satisfy all 2^k−1 inequalities simultaneously.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed universal statement, or its logical negation with the same quantifier order. Failure of one algorithm for producing b, or failure of obtaining the scaling by conditioning the original strings on an auxiliary string, is not a refutation. The logarithmic slack is part of the proposition, not a numerical-estimation tolerance.

title: Optimal quantum query complexity of uniformity testing
reason: Uniformity is a canonical statistical testing task; its full quantum query tradeoff measures a fundamental advantage of coherent sample access.
formal: Determine Q(d,ε), the optimal worst-case quantum query complexity of distinguishing p=u_d from d_TV(p,u_d)>ε with success probability at least 0.99, up to universal constant factors jointly for all integers d≥2 and real 0<ε≤1/4. Access is to an arbitrary distribution synthesizer with the precise oracle convention below.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(d,ε) and absolute constants a,A>0 such that a g(d,ε)≤Q(d,ε)≤A g(d,ε) throughout the stated domain. Prove both bounds uniformly over its two parameters and all valid oracle implementations. A formula or certified evaluation rule may specify g; merely renaming Q is insufficient. This is an asymptotic query bound up to multiplicative constants, not pointwise additive 0.01 accuracy.

title: Optimal multiclass regret versus Littlestone dimension
reason: The minimax regret of every multiclass hypothesis family tests whether Littlestone dimension alone captures online prediction difficulty, even with infinitely many labels.
formal: Determine R(d,T)=sup{R_T(H): H is a nonempty multiclass hypothesis class with L(H)≤d}, up to universal constant factors, for integers T≥d≥1. The supremum ranges over arbitrary instance and label sets, including infinite label sets. R_T(H) is the full-label online minimax regret defined below; learners have no computational-efficiency restriction.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(d,T) and constants a,A>0 independent of both parameters, all label sets and all hypothesis classes, and prove a g(d,T)≤R(d,T)≤A g(d,T) for every integer T≥d≥1. Lower bounds may use families of classes; a worst-case class need not attain the supremum. This is an asymptotic regret target with multiplicative constants, not additive 0.01 error.

title: Removing low-influence directions from convex sets
reason: Dimension-free stability of negligible Gaussian influence would give a general geometric meaning to an irrelevant direction in a convex set.
formal: Does there exist a function τ:(0,1)→[0,1] with lim_{ε→0⁺}τ(ε)=0 such that the following holds for every n≥1, every centrally symmetric convex Borel set K⊆ℝⁿ, every unit vector v and every ε∈(0,1)? If Inf_v[K]≤ε, then there exists a centrally symmetric convex Borel set C⊆v⊥ such that γₙ(K △ (C+ℝv))≤τ(ε). The same τ must work in all dimensions and for all such sets and directions.
answer_criterion: Prove a single modulus τ tending to zero that bounds the Gaussian approximation error uniformly over the stated sets, dimensions and directions, or prove that no such modulus exists. Equivalently for a negative answer, exhibit a sequence with directional influence tending to zero while its Gaussian distance from every symmetric convex cylinder in that direction stays bounded below by a positive constant. A dimension-dependent modulus or a cylinder in some other direction does not suffice.

title: Memory–sample tradeoffs for noisy parity learning
reason: The memory cost of noisy parity learning separates information retained from samples from computation time and exposes a basic resource cost of noise.
formal: Do there exist absolute constants c₁,c₂>0 and n₀ such that, for every integer n≥n₀, every 0<ε<1/2 and every one-pass learner recovering a uniformly random x∈{0,1}^n with probability at least 2/3 from the noisy parity samples defined below, its worst-case memory S and maximum sample count T satisfy S≥c₁n²/ε² or T≥2^{c₂n}? Constants are independent of n, ε and the learner, and ε may tend to zero with n. This states the bounded-error recovery interpretation of Conjecture 1; it does not additionally require a lower bound at exponentially small success probability.
answer_criterion: Prove the universal bounded-error memory/sample tradeoff with constants uniform in ε, or refute that asymptotic claim by showing that no such constants can work. A bound Ω(n²/ε), a result only for constant ε, or a lower bound in a restricted statistical-query model does not settle the proposed dependence on noise.

title: Polynomial exact metric sparsifiers with a crossing-edge budget
reason: One small edge set preserving every metric-labeling query is a broad graph-compression principle, with substantially more content than a bound for one cut objective.
formal: Do there exist absolute constants C,c>0 such that the following holds? For every finite simple undirected unweighted graph G=(V,E), terminal set T⊆V of size r, and integer p≥0, there is a set Z⊆E with |Z|≤C(1+p+r)^c having this universal property: for every finite nonempty label set D, every metric μ:D×D→R_{≥0}, and every terminal labeling τ:T→D, if there exists a labeling λ:V→D extending τ with at most p crossing edges, then some labeling λ* of minimum μ-cost among all such budget-feasible extensions has all its crossing edges in Z. The same Z must work simultaneously for every D,μ,τ and depends only on G,T,p. This is the polynomial-size version of the contraction-based metric-sparsifier property in the source’s Theorem 22; that theorem’s earlier quasipolynomial upper-bound claim was later retracted.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated universal polynomial bound, or refute it by showing that no fixed constants C,c can bound the required retained edges over all G,T,p. A negative result must respect the quantifier order: every candidate small Z must fail for some label set, metric and terminal labeling with a feasible budgeted extension. Hardness of finding a small Z does not disprove its existence. Bounds for one fixed metric, a fixed number of labels, ordinary terminal cut values, or approximate values do not settle this target.

title: Exact exponential-time equivalence for nonnegative Boolean Max-CSP
reason: A degree-based exact-time classification would organize all finite NP-hard Boolean Max-CSP languages with nonnegative weights under one invariant.
formal: Does the following extension of the source’s degree-based classification hold? For every fixed finite Boolean constraint language Γ that is neither 0-valid, 1-valid, nor 2-monotone, let d=deg(Γ). For every fixed real α>1, if Max CSP(Γ,N,c) has an exact deterministic algorithm running in αⁿn^{O(1)} time for every fixed constant c≥1, must Max d-CNF-SAT with nonnegative integer weights of total weight at most nᶜ also have an exact deterministic αⁿn^{O(1)}-time algorithm for every fixed c≥1? The same base α is required. Algorithms and polynomial factors may depend on Γ,α,c. This formulates the conclusion’s speedup question as extending Theorem 6.2 to all NP-hard nonnegative-weight languages; tractable languages are explicitly excluded.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed implication for every eligible fixed language Γ and every α>1, retaining the same exponential base and the all-c weight convention, or refute it by a language and a rigorously established failure of that implication. A theorem comparing only whether both problems are NP-hard, or comparing compression sizes or exponential rates after a constant-factor increase in variable count, does not establish the stated base-preserving classification.

title: Non-clashing teaching dimension versus VC dimension
reason: The sharp universal relation between VC dimension and non-clashing teaching compares two basic notions of information needed to identify concepts.
formal: For every finite set X and every nonempty concept class C⊆2ˣ, is NCTD(C)≤VC(C)? Equivalently, if C has VC dimension d, does there exist a teaching map assigning at most d correctly labeled examples to each concept such that no two distinct concepts are mutually consistent with one another’s assigned examples? Both positive and negative examples are allowed. The target constant is exactly one, not merely a bound O(d).
answer_criterion: Prove the exact inequality for every finite concept class by establishing existence of a valid map of maximum size at most its VC dimension, or give a finite concept class and a proof that every non-clashing teaching map has larger maximum size. A quadratic bound or even a larger-constant linear bound is insufficient. A separation for positive-only maps, another teaching model, or an algorithmic hardness result for finding maps does not refute this existence statement.

title: Proper unlabeled compression of ample classes
reason: Optimal proper unlabeled compression of every ample class is a substantial structural case of the central sample-compression programme.
formal: Does every nonempty ample concept class C⊆{0,1}ᵁ on a finite domain U admit a proper unlabeled sample compression scheme of size at most d=VC(C)? Precisely, do there exist maps κ:RS(C)→{A⊆U:|A|≤d} and ρ:{A⊆U:|A|≤d}→C such that, for every realizable labeled partial sample s, κ(s)⊆dom(s) and ρ(κ(s)) agrees with every label in s? The stored object is only an unordered subset of the sample’s input points. The bound is d, not an unspecified multiple of d.
answer_criterion: Prove existence of the two maps with the stated d-point bound for every finite nonempty ample class, or give an ample class with a proof that no such pair of maps exists. A scheme retaining labels, returning a hypothesis outside C, storing extra information, or exceeding d points does not meet the target. A scheme that handles only full concepts rather than every realizable partial sample is also insufficient. Failure of a proposed corner-peeling construction alone does not refute existence of a compression scheme.

title: Approximate polynomial satisfiability in AM under GRH
reason: The complexity of approaching a common polynomial zero is a basic question about algebraic closure and border computation; AM versus the known polynomial-space bound is a qualitative gap.
formal: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, is approximate polynomial satisfiability for rational-coefficient arithmetic circuits in AM? An instance consists of division-free circuits computing f₁,…,f_m∈ℚ[x₁,…,x_n]. It is a YES instance if, for every real η>0, there is a point a∈ℂⁿ with max_i |f_i(a)|<η; otherwise it is a NO instance. Equivalently, for every polynomial A∈ℚ[y₁,…,y_m], the identity A(f₁,…,f_m)=0 must imply A(0,…,0)=0. This equivalent decision predicate is AnnAtZero. Ask for one uniform public-coin protocol with verifier time, random-tape length and prover-message length polynomial in the full binary input length, with completeness at least 2/3 and soundness at most 1/3 on every instance.
answer_criterion: Prove, under GRH, that one AM protocol satisfying the stated bounds decides every encoded instance, or refute the inclusion under the same assumption. A protocol only for exact common-root existence, algebraic dependence, bounded-degree special cases, or finite fields does not establish the target. A PSPACE algorithm or a test at one fixed positive numerical tolerance is insufficient. Failure of a proposed protocol is not a proof that APS is outside AM.

title: Limiting optimized QAOA energy in the SK model
reason: The limiting optimized energy of QAOA asks whether a central quantum optimization ansatz can reach the statistical-mechanics optimum after taking the infinite-instance limit.
formal: Determine A=sup_{p≥1} sup_{γ,β∈ℝ^p} a_p(γ,β), where a_p(γ,β)=lim_{n→∞} n^{−1} E_J[⟨ψ_{p,J}(γ,β)|H_J|ψ_{p,J}(γ,β)⟩] for the Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Hamiltonian and QAOA state defined below. The benchmark requires absolute error at most 1/100 in energy per spin.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous value a and a Lean proof that |a−A|≤1/100, or certified lower and upper bounds of width at most 1/50 with the midpoint as answer. Exact determination also qualifies. Merely restating the defining supremum, reporting floating-point optimization at finitely many depths, or interchanging depth and instance-size limits is insufficient. Equality with Π* is a stronger possible answer, not assumed by the target.

title: Optimal randomized competitive ratio of weighted k-server
reason: The optimal randomized cost of heterogeneous servers is a central online resource-allocation question; the recent singly-exponential breakthrough leaves a substantial quantitative frontier.
formal: Determine the asymptotic growth of R_w(k), the optimal randomized competitive ratio of the weighted k-server problem over all finite uniform metrics, up to universal multiplicative constants as the integer k tends to infinity. Use an oblivious request adversary and expected online cost, as defined below.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(k) and constants a,A>0,k₀ such that a g(k)≤R_w(k)≤A g(k) for every integer k≥k₀, proving both bounds in the specified randomized model. Constants must not depend on metric size or weights. An improvement for one algorithm, fixed weight ratios or a bounded number of locations does not by itself determine this worst-case function. Precision is multiplicative constant factors in R_w, not additive 0.01 and not merely constant factors in its logarithm.

title: Downward self-reducibility of integer factoring
reason: Downward self-reducibility of integer factoring asks whether a canonical arithmetic search problem has the recursive structure common to complete problems.
formal: Is there one deterministic oracle Turing machine A and a polynomial p such that, for every integer N≥2 of binary length n, A outputs the complete prime factorization of N within p(n) steps, using a factoring oracle only on integers M≥2 whose binary length is strictly less than n?
answer_criterion: Prove existence of the uniform polynomial-time reduction or its logical negation. Factoring using smaller numerical values of the same bit length, arbitrary smaller circuits for a factoring relation, or an exponential-time recursion does not meet the stated definition. The output need not be a decimal expansion of the input; its prime-power representation is explicit.

title: Does NP-hardness of MCSP imply circuit lower bounds for EXP?
reason: Whether ordinary NP-hardness of circuit minimization entails exponential-time circuit lower bounds is a central connection between metacomplexity and nonuniform lower bounds.
formal: If the Minimum Circuit Size Problem is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, must EXP⊄P/poly? The hypothesis uses unrestricted ordinary polynomial-time reductions, with no locality, uniform-AC⁰ or naturalness promise.
answer_criterion: Prove the conditional implication or its logical negation in these exact reduction and circuit models. Deriving only EXP≠ZPP or EXP≠NP∩P/poly is a weaker consequence. A theorem for a restricted reduction class or for partial, promise or approximate circuit minimization does not prove the stated implication.

title: Sharp low-degree Fourier weight of halfspaces
reason: A sharp universal low-degree Fourier inequality for all halfspaces describes the spectral structure of a foundational Boolean function class.
formal: For every integer n≥1 and every linear threshold function f:{−1,1}^n→{−1,1}, is W^{≤1}(f)=f̂(∅)²+Σ_{i=1}^n f̂({i})²≥2/π?
answer_criterion: Prove the exact universal inequality or give a threshold function with a rigorous proof that its low-degree weight is strictly less than 2/π. Approximation of the extremal constant to 0.01 would not settle this universal proposition. An algorithm for approximating that constant is already known; the retained target is the source’s sharp inequality.

title: Optimal size of four-additive graph spanners
reason: The +4 additive-spanner regime is the classical remaining constant-error sparsity-exponent gap, making it a central distance-compression problem rather than a peripheral parameter choice.
formal: Determine s₄(n)=max_G min_H |E(H)| up to universal multiplicative constants for integers n≥2, where G ranges over connected simple undirected unweighted graphs on n vertices and H ranges over their spanning subgraphs satisfying d_H(u,v)≤d_G(u,v)+4 for all vertices u,v.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(n), constants a,A>0 and n₀ such that a g(n)≤s₄(n)≤A g(n) for every integer n≥n₀. Prove a universal existence upper bound and a matching worst-case lower bound. Polynomial exponents alone do not settle this constant-factor target if a growing logarithmic gap remains. This is an asymptotic extremal-size question, not an additive 0.01 estimate of an integer function.

title: Scholz–Brauer conjecture
reason: The Scholz–Brauer conjecture is a longstanding universal law proposed for optimal addition chains, linking a basic arithmetic complexity measure across all exponents.
formal: For every positive integer n, is ℓ(2ⁿ−1)≤n−1+ℓ(n), where ℓ(m) is the minimum length of an addition chain for m?
answer_criterion: Prove the inequality for every positive integer n, or give an integer n together with rigorous bounds on the two minimum lengths showing ℓ(2ⁿ−1)>n−1+ℓ(n). A positive proof may establish existence of the required chains without an efficient algorithm for finding a shortest chain. Equality is not required. Restricted-chain results, a finite verification range, and validity for a density-one set of integers are weaker than the universal assertion.

title: Boolean dimension of posets with planar cover graphs
reason: A constant-size Boolean description of every order with a planar cover graph would explain how planar local structure controls global order information.
formal: Does there exist an integer d≥1 such that every finite poset P=(V,<) with a planar undirected cover graph admits strict total orders L_1,...,L_d on V and a Boolean function φ:{0,1}^d→{0,1} satisfying, for all distinct x,y∈V, x<y if and only if φ(1[x<_(L_1)y],...,1[x<_(L_d)y])=1?
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.

title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
reason: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture is a classical universal expansion principle for arbitrary oriented graphs, with broad extremal significance.
formal: Does every finite nonempty oriented graph D contain a vertex v for which |N⁺⁺(v)|≥|N⁺(v)|, where N⁺(v) consists of vertices at directed distance one from v and N⁺⁺(v) consists of vertices at directed distance exactly two?
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.

title: Optimal multilinear-formula size of the permanent
reason: The optimal multilinear formula size of the permanent concerns a canonical explicit algebraic lower bound with a qualitative quasipolynomial-to-exponential gap.
formal: Determine the growth of log₂ F(n) up to universal multiplicative constants as n→∞, where F(n) is the minimum size of a multilinear arithmetic formula over ℂ computing perm_n. Equivalently, find a positive function g(n) and constants a,A>0,n₀ such that 2^{a g(n)}≤F(n)≤2^{A g(n)} for every integer n≥n₀.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function g(n) and prove the two bounds displayed in the statement for the specified formula model, with constants independent of n. Merely restating log₂ F(n), proving a bound for constant depth or prohibiting cancellation adds restrictions not present here. This is an asymptotic exponent target, not a pointwise 0.01 approximation. The original exponential lower-bound conjecture would give g(n)=n, using the known exponential-size upper bound.
